key_insight: In older adults, women showed greater activation in several visual, limbic, and thalamic regions during worry induction, suggesting sex-related differences in the brain networks engaged by worry and reappraisal.
clinical_relevance: These findings may help explain why chronic, hard-to-control worry is more common in older women and could inform future studies of sex-specific emotional regulation and anxiety-related brain patterns.
method: 131 older adults completed an fMRI worry induction and reappraisal task
Voxel-wise t-tests compared sex differences across brain activation contrasts
Regression tested how worry severity and regulation strategies related to activity in significant regions
evidence_signal: The analysis found significant sex differences in task-related activation, with greater reappraisal use linked to less severe worry and specific brain regions showing sex-differential associations with reappraisal.
watch_item: This is an observational neuroimaging study, so the results show association rather than causation and may not generalize beyond the studied older-adult sample.
paper_title: Sex Differences in Neural Activity during Worry Induction and Reappraisal in Late Life
